claims.text: At low applied fields, the magnetocaloric response of rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys is predominantly governed by the degree of local lattice distortion.
Local lattice distortion enhances spin-lattice coupling.
Enhanced spin-lattice coupling broadens the magnetic transition while retaining continuous, near-second-order character.
A broadened continuous magnetic transition enables a large isothermal entropy change at fields below 1 T.
A broadened continuous magnetic transition limits thermal and magnetic hysteresis.
The proposed distortion-mediated response permits rapid phonon-mediated heat transfer while maintaining mechanical stability.
Replacing part of one constituent with 3–5 at.% of an atom having a substantially different atomic radius will systematically tune local lattice distortion.
Enhanced local lattice distortion and chemical heterogeneity modify local exchange interactions between magnetic moments.
Distortion-induced perturbations of interatomic distances strengthen spin-lattice coupling.
Stronger spin-lattice coupling broadens and smoothens the magnetic transition.
Enhanced phonon scattering in the disordered matrix sustains rapid heat exchange.
Increasing lattice distortion through the proposed substitution preserves the alloy's mechanical integrity.
Relative to the baseline, the substituted alloy will exhibit a larger isothermal entropy change at applied fields below 1 T.
Relative to the baseline, the substituted alloy will exhibit reduced magnetization-field hysteresis.
Relative to the baseline, the substituted alloy will exhibit a faster transient thermal response.
The substitution will not significantly degrade elastic modulus or fracture resistance.
The proposed mechanism is limited to single-phase disordered alloys near room temperature and applied fields below 1 T.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to sharp first-order magnetostructural transitions.
The proposed mechanism may not apply when substitution produces secondary phases.
